\label{lesson:PA-R161-swim-again}



\begin{quote}
Hear \textbf{to swim}. {[}PAUSE 4s{]} Say the earlier Punjabi word before the model: \textbf{\pa{ਤਰਨਾ}} (\emph{tarnā}).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear \textbf{\pa{ਤਰਨਾ}}. {[}PAUSE 4s{]} Recall its old meaning, \textbf{to swim}. Now hear \textbf{to swim} and say \textbf{\pa{ਤਰਨਾ}} before the spoken model. No sentence or new grammar is needed.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
One last cue: \textbf{to swim}. {[}PAUSE 4s{]} Recall \textbf{\pa{ਤਰਨਾ}}. Listen and retry once if it does not come back. This is untimed vocabulary retrieval, not scored A1 writing or mock evidence.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਵਰਤਣਾ} (vartṇā)}{ਵਰਤਣਾ (vartṇā)}]{An old word for using}

\label{lesson:PA-R161-use-again}



\begin{quote}
Hear \textbf{to use}. {[}PAUSE 4s{]} Say the old word before the model: \textbf{\pa{ਵਰਤਣਾ}} (\emph{vartṇā}).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Pause after each familiar meaning, then hear its model:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{to call} — {[}PAUSE 4s{]} \textbf{\pa{ਬੁਲਾਉਣਾ}} (\emph{bulāuṇā}).
  \item \textbf{to swim} — {[}PAUSE 4s{]} \textbf{\pa{ਤਰਨਾ}} (\emph{tarnā}).
  \item \textbf{to use} — {[}PAUSE 4s{]} \textbf{\pa{ਵਰਤਣਾ}} (\emph{vartṇā}).
  \item \textbf{to climb} — {[}PAUSE 4s{]} \textbf{\pa{ਚੜ੍ਹਨਾ}} (\emph{caṛhnā}).
\end{itemize}

Only the order of these four old words has changed.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Hear \textbf{to climb}, \textbf{to use}, \textbf{to call}, then \textbf{to swim}. Pause after each cue and recall its Punjabi word before the model: \textbf{\pa{ਚੜ੍ਹਨਾ}}, \textbf{\pa{ਵਰਤਣਾ}}, \textbf{\pa{ਬੁਲਾਉਣਾ}}, \textbf{\pa{ਤਰਨਾ}}. Revisit only the old word you missed.
